title: Saif Ali Khan Says Shah Rukh Offered Him 'Main Hoon Na' — Farah Khan Says That Never Happened
excerpt: A 22-year-old Bollywood casting mystery resurfaces just as the two Khans reunite in 'Kartavya' on Netflix. The director is not amused.
body:
There are Bollywood "what if" stories, and then there's this: Saif Ali Khan has revealed that Shah Rukh Khan personally called him to offer a role in Main Hoon Na back in 2004. Director Farah Khan's response? "First I'm hearing this."

The duelling claims have surfaced as Saif and SRK gear up for their much-anticipated reunion in Kartavya, which began streaming on Netflix on May 15 — making the timing either brilliant promotion or spectacularly awkward, depending on whom you believe.

The Story According to Saif

In a recent interview, Saif described the incident with characteristic charm. Shah Rukh Khan, who produced Main Hoon Na through Red Chillies Entertainment, apparently called Saif directly to offer him a role. Saif was intrigued — he called it a "wonderful production" — but then received a follow-up call from Farah Khan herself, who effectively shut it down.

"Shah Rukh called me for Main Hoon Na... then Farah Khan called and said no," Saif recalled, adding that he found the whole situation "very cool" in retrospect.

The role Saif was reportedly considered for remains unspecified, though fans have speculated it could have been the military officer villain eventually played by Suniel Shetty, or possibly Zayed Khan's role as the younger brother.

Farah's Flat Denial

Farah Khan — who directed Main Hoon Na as her debut film and has spoken extensively about its chaotic casting process over the years — wasn't having it. "First I hear about this," she responded, effectively dismissing the story as either misremembered or embellished.

This is consistent with Farah's well-documented accounts of how Main Hoon Na was cast. She's previously recalled that "except Shah Rukh Khan, all other casting was a nightmare" — describing last-minute dropouts, replacements, and the kind of creative friction that defines Bollywood productions. Hrithik Roshan walked out. Ayesha Takia was replaced. Kamal Haasan declined. Rakhi Sawant auditioned in a burka and then removed it to reveal a bikini.

In that context, the Saif story is either another chapter in the film's legendary casting chaos, or a detail that slipped through the cracks of a very busy production.

Why NRIs Care About a 22-Year-Old Film

Main Hoon Na occupies a specific place in the diaspora imagination. Released in 2004, it arrived during peak Bollywood nostalgia era — when SRK was the undisputed king, college campus films were the genre du jour, and every NRI household had a DVD copy alongside Kal Ho Naa Ho and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham.

For Indians abroad, the film's patriotic themes, campus romance, and SRK's dual-identity storyline (an army officer posing as a college student) resonated with the diaspora experience of living between two worlds. It's the kind of movie that still plays at community Diwali events and cultural nights across North America and the UK.

The revelation that Saif — who was already a star by 2004 — almost joined that cast adds a delicious parallel-universe dimension. Would a Saif-SRK pairing in 2004 have changed the trajectory of either career? Probably not. But it's exactly the kind of Bollywood insider story that fuels group-chat debates from New Jersey to Dubai.

The Kartavya Connection

The timing of this revelation is impossible to ignore. Kartavya, streaming now on Netflix, marks the first time Saif and Shah Rukh have shared substantial screen time since Kal Ho Naa Ho in 2003. The film, produced by SRK's Red Chillies, brings the two together in what's being marketed as a high-stakes thriller — a far cry from the campus fun of Main Hoon Na.

Whether Saif's casting story is promotional chatter or genuine memory, it's done its job: people are talking about both Main Hoon Na and Kartavya in the same breath.

Kartavya is now streaming on Netflix worldwide.
